rationale: Ground truth is sparse (LGTM approval plus four style/organization nitpicks resolved amicably), and neither candidate surfaces those specific concerns, so recall is low for both. Both independently converge on the same well-grounded blocking bug (double-seeding num_stale_output_tokens via _replace_streaming_session), which cross-validates that finding for each. Beyond that, X makes two claims (randomize_inputs still leaking via env var, VLLM_CACHE_ROOT race) that directly contradict Y's explicit 'validated' checks on the same code, plus an unverifiable CI-red claim, hurting X's precision. Y's structured validated/confirmed format with quoted evidence per claim, plus a well-evidenced systemic finding (arg_utils registry override leaving ~10 other model classes unhardened, listed by file:line), is comparably actionable and slightly more reliable overall.
